claim: All-trans retinoic acid (atRA) induces synaptic plasticity in acute brain slices prepared from the mouse and human neocortex.
source: Previously we showed that the vitamin A metabolite all-trans retinoic acid (atRA) induces synaptic plasticity in acute brain slices prepared from the mouse and human neocortex (Lenz et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Lenz et al., 2021).

claim: Distinct effects of atRA on excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission have been reported depending on the brain region studied.
source: Depending on the brain region studied, distinct effects of atRA on excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission have been reported.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about regional differences in atRA effects.

claim: Intraperitoneal injections of atRA (10 mg/kg) in adult C57BL/6J mice were used to study the effects of atRA on excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission in the mouse fascia dentata.
source: Here, we used intraperitoneal injections of atRA (10 mg/kg) in adult C57BL/6J mice to study the effects of atRA on excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission in the mouse fascia dentata—a brain region implicated in memory acquisition.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The fascia dentata is a brain region implicated in memory acquisition.
source: Here, we used intraperitoneal injections of atRA (10 mg/kg) in adult C57BL/6J mice to study the effects of atRA on excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission in the mouse fascia dentata—a brain region implicated in memory acquisition.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about the function of the fascia dentata.

claim: No major changes in synaptic transmission were observed in the ventral hippocampus 6 hr after atRA administration.
source: No major changes in synaptic transmission were observed in the ventral hippocampus while a significant increase in both spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic current frequencies and synapse numbers were evident in the dorsal hippocampus 6 hr after atRA administration.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: A significant increase in both spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic current frequencies and synapse numbers were evident in the dorsal hippocampus 6 hr after atRA administration.
source: No major changes in synaptic transmission were observed in the ventral hippocampus while a significant increase in both spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic current frequencies and synapse numbers were evident in the dorsal hippocampus 6 hr after atRA administration.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: The intrinsic properties of hippocampal dentate granule cells were not significantly different after atRA treatment.
source: The intrinsic properties of hippocampal dentate granule cells were not significantly different and hippocampal transcriptome analysis revealed no essential neuronal changes upon atRA treatment.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: Hippocampal transcriptome analysis revealed no essential neuronal changes upon atRA treatment.
source: The intrinsic properties of hippocampal dentate granule cells were not significantly different and hippocampal transcriptome analysis revealed no essential neuronal changes upon atRA treatment.

claim: Systemic atRA treatment improves the ability of dentate granule cells to express LTP.
source: Indeed, in vivo long-term potentiation (LTP) experiments demonstrated that systemic atRA treatment improves the ability of dentate granule cells to express LTP.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from in vivo LTP experiments.

claim: The plasticity-promoting effects of atRA were not observed in synaptopodin-deficient mice.
source: The plasticity-promoting effects of atRA were not observed in synaptopodin-deficient mice, therefore, extending our previous results regarding the relevance of synaptopodin in atRA-mediated synaptic strengthening in the mouse prefrontal cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from synaptopodin-deficient mice.

claim: Synaptopodin is relevant in atRA-mediated synaptic strengthening in the mouse prefrontal cortex.
source: The plasticity-promoting effects of atRA were not observed in synaptopodin-deficient mice, therefore, extending our previous results regarding the relevance of synaptopodin in atRA-mediated synaptic strengthening in the mouse prefrontal cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous results.

claim: atRA mediates synaptopodin-dependent metaplasticity in mouse dentate granule cells.
source: Taken together, our data show that atRA mediates synaptopodin-dependent metaplasticity in mouse dentate granule cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: Adaptive processes in synaptic sites of the central nervous system are fundamental to normal brain function.

claim: The vitamin A derivative all-trans retinoic acid (atRA) is one of the key mediators of excitatory and inhibitory synaptic plasticity among plasticity-related signaling molecules.
